newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses end week with sharp losses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses end week with sharp losses.

text.p: European stocks fell sharply on Friday as another wave of program-selling on Wall Street touched raw nerves and added to fears the bull run in world markets might be slowing.

On currency markets, the dollar ended the week shy of new 31-month highs against the mark and well off a 47-month peak above 120 yen as uncertainty about the reaction of authorities to the recent dollar rally crept into the market.

Most of the action was in equity markets. In a dramatic reversal after closing at fresh peaks on Thursday, major European bourses ended about 1.25 percent down, rattled by Wall Street's weak performance.
London, Frankfurt and Paris all opened in the minus column after Wall Street tumbled from record levels on Thursday, hit by sell programs triggered by a reverse of sentiment in the futures markets.

Investors were shaken when New York opened on Friday and promptly chalked up additional losses, again because of sell programs, igniting fears that Wall Street could be on the verge of a major correction.
London's FTSE index ended 1.23 points lower at 4218.8 after hitting a record close on Thursday. A profits warning from one of Britain's leading supermarket chains also undermined market confidence.
Although every stock in the FTSE 100 blue chip index was marked lower at one point, some traders were reluctant to call an end to the New Year rally.
"Fundamentally, we are still bullish of the UK market," said Corey Miller, equities strategist at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
"Markets on both sides of the Atlantic have performed strongly so it's to be expected that we now have a bit of profit-taking."

In Frankfurt, stocks on the computerised IBIS index suffered the biggest drop of the day, registering a 1.8 percent fall at the close. Floor trade, which ended before New York opened, was down only 1.16 percent.
But some dealers said it was not the large-scale correction many had feared. "This is not a catastrophe," said one, "It's being seen by some as an opportunity to buy."
Paris had a bad session. Stocks showed a loss of 1.26 precent at the close as investors, with a nervous eye on Wall Street, took profits.
"I do not see any reason for people to panic. We have had quite a run. It all went up very quickly, and it is now time to pause and take profits," a broker said.
On Thursday, French shares closed at a record of 2,461.25 points on the CAC-40 index, which has risen from 2,193.70 on December 17.
On the currency front, the dollar had a volatile day, falling in European trade after an overnight jump above 120 yen in Asia amid a spate of contradictory Japanese comments.

Japanese government reports that yen weakness would not be detrimental to the economy propelled the dollar as high as 120.15 yen, only to be met immediately with official protests about the yen slide and rumours of Bank of Japan intervention.
Sentiment in favour of the dollar's strength against the mark was was also tempered by some brisk German inflation data and cautious Bundesbank statements.

"There's growing interest about what the Japanese and German authorities will tolerate in terms of further dollar strength and there may well be an assymetry of views here," said Julian Jessop, economist at Nikko Europe.

Jessop said the Japanese seem happy with a weaker yen but not with excessive volatility, while the Bundesbank may start to grow wary of a weaker mark given the latest inflation data, particularly import price inflation.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 118.96 yen and 1.6287 marks in late European trade after Thursday's levels of 119.50 and 1.6380.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 52.7 points lower at 4,218.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 30.91 at 2,430.34.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 35.22 at 2,998.24.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed higher at $353.35 an ounce, compared to Thursday's close at $349.45. Silver ended two cents higher at $4.91.
